bottom_line: In APPRAISE-2, apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs placebo added to standard antiplatelet therapy after acute coronary syndrome did not significantly reduce the primary outcome (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11) and increased TIMI major bleeding (hazard ratio with apixaban, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46).
implications: With 279/3705 (7.5%) vs 293/3687 (7.9%) for cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke (hazard ratio 0.95; 95% CI, 0.80 to 1.11; P = 0.51), the document supports that apixaban did not show a statistically significant reduction in recurrent ischemic events in this trial. With TIMI major bleeding 46/3673 (1.3%) vs 18/3642 (0.5%) (hazard ratio 2.59; 95% CI, 1.50 to 4.46; P = 0.001), it supports that adding apixaban increased major bleeding; the text also reports more fatal bleeding (5 vs. 0) and intracranial bleeding (12 vs. 3) with apixaban. Because the trial was stopped early, the document states that certainty about efficacy conclusions is limited.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in ACS patients with additional ischemic risk factors, testing apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs placebo on top of antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote:
We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial comparing apixaban, at a dose of 5 mg twice daily, with placebo, in addition to standard anti-
platelet therapy, in patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome and at least two additional risk factors

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.
major_points.quote:
The primary efficacy outcome was the composite
of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or
ischemic stroke.

major_points.text: Trial was stopped early due to excess clinically important bleeding without counterbalancing reduction in ischemic events.
major_points.quote:
The trial was terminated prematurely after recruitment of 7392 patients because of an
increase in major bleeding events with apixaban in the absence of a counterbalanc-
ing reduction in recurrent ischemic events.

major_points.text: Intracranial and fatal bleeding events were more frequent with apixaban than placebo.
major_points.quote:
A greater number of intracranial and fatal bleeding
events occurred with apixaban than with placebo.

absolute_effects.text: Fatal bleeding: 5 (0.1) with apixaban vs 0 with placebo.
Intracranial bleeding: 12 (0.3) with apixaban vs 3 (0.1) with placebo.

harms.text: Fatal bleeding and intracranial bleeding were more frequent with apixaban than placebo.
harms.quote:
Among the patients receiv-
ing apixaban, as compared with those receiving
placebo, there were more events of fatal bleeding
(5 vs. 0), intracranial bleeding (12 vs. 3)

harms.text: Patients receiving apixaban received more transfusions than placebo.
harms.quote:
Patients receiving
apixaban received more transfusions than did pa-
tients receiving placebo (144 [3.9%] vs. 73 [2.0%]).

harms.text: Serious adverse events were similar in both groups (24.3% vs 24.3%).
harms.quote:
The frequencies of serious adverse events and
overall adverse events were similar in the apixaban
group and the placebo group (24.3% and 59.0%,
respectively, in the apixaban group and 24.3% and
57.7%, respectively, in the placebo group).

harms.text: More patients stopped study drug early in apixaban vs placebo (23.5% vs 20.5%).
harms.quote:
863 of the 3673 patients who received at least one
dose of apixaban (23.5%) and 746 of the 3642 who
received at least one dose of placebo (20.5%) stopped
taking the study drug before the end of the trial
(P = 0.002).

inclusion_criteria.text: Acute coronary syndrome (myocardial infarction with/without ST-segment elevation, or unstable angina) within the previous 7 days, with ≥10 minutes ischemic symptoms at rest plus biomarker elevation or dynamic ST-segment changes.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
The main inclusion criterion for the trial was an
acute coronary syndrome (myocardial infarction,
with or without ST-segment elevation, or unstable
angina) within the previous 7 days, with symptoms
of myocardial ischemia lasting 10 minutes or more

inclusion_criteria.text: Symptoms plus either elevated cardiac biomarkers or dynamic ST-segment depression/elevation ≥0.1 mV.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
with the patient at rest plus either elevated levels of
cardiac biomarkers or dynamic ST-segment depres-
sion or elevation of 0.1 mV or more.

inclusion_criteria.text: Eligible if clinically stable and receiving standard treatment including aspirin or aspirin plus any P2Y12-receptor antagonist.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Patients who
met this criterion were eligible for the study if their
condition was clinically stable and they were re-
ceiving standard treatment after the acute coronary
syndrome, including aspirin or aspirin plus any
P2Y12-receptor antagonist.

inclusion_criteria.text: Required to have two or more prespecified high-risk characteristics (e.g., age ≥65, diabetes, prior MI, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, HF/LVEF<40%, impaired renal function, or no revascularization).

also required to have two or more of the following
high-risk characteristics: an age of at least 65 years,
diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction within the
previous 5 years, cerebrovascular disease, periph-
eral vascular disease

analysis_methods.text: Intended treatment period was basis for efficacy analyses; actual treatment period was basis for safety analyses.
analysis_methods.quote:
The intended treatment period,
starting on the
day of randomization and ending at the efficacy
cutoff date (November 18, 2010), is the basis for
the efficacy analyses. The actual treatment period,
starting on the date the first dose of study drug
was administered and ending 2 days after the last
dose of study drug was administered, is the basis
for the analyses of safety.

analysis_methods.text: Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by baseline antiplatelet therapy (single vs dual).
analysis_methods.quote:
Efficacy and bleeding outcomes were analyzed
with the use of a Cox proportional-hazards model
that included the assigned study group as a co-
variate and that was stratified according to anti-
platelet therapy (single or dual) at baseline.

analysis_methods.text: Estimated 80% power to detect 20% relative risk reduction at one-sided alpha 0.005 and 93% power at one-sided alpha 0.025.

we es-

ban as compared with placebo at a one-sided al-
pha level of 0.005 and 93% power to detect the
same reduction in risk at a one-sided alpha level
of 0.025.

criticisms.text: Uncertainty remains regarding effect on ischemic events due to early stopping and fewer than planned ischemic events.
criticisms.quote:
Because this trial was stopped early owing to the
increase in bleeding events, with fewer ischemic
events having occurred than the number planned,
uncertainty remains regarding the effect of apixa-
ban on ischemic events.
